liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Not Fade Away** (2 reviews): Not Fade Away is blistering, as are Johnny B. Goode and Don't Ease Me In; Space into Not Fade Away features cool keyboard and wah guitar effects [22][23]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Jack Straw into Franklin's Tower and the back end are powerful [16]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Let It Grow into Deal is highlighted as a strong, great moment [16]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Estimated Prophet into The Other One is likely the show's highlight [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-06-20.sbd.bertha.tetzeli.fix-25468.73846.reflac.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 167 min; rated 4.9/5 by 10 [1]
- **gd1980-06-20.mtx.seamons.92783.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 165 min; rated 4.6/5 by 5 [2]
- **gd80-06-20.sbd.donohue.17268.sbefixed.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 164 min; rated 3.5/5 by 6 [3]. Said about its sound: Soundboard has clean vocals, though hi-hat and bass drum are sometimes overpowering [15]
- **gd1980-06-20.sbd.miller.bertha.25468.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 170 min; rated 1.67/5 by 3 [5]
- **gd1980-06-20.sbd.miller.25469.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 171 min [6]
- **gd80-06-20.akg-claridge-healy.vernon.20205.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 163 min; rated 4.71/5 by 17 [9]. Said about its sound: Listener describes the audience recording as excellent, capturing melancholy and joy; Sound is good, but the recording could use a bit more Phil; Sound quality is fierce for a 1980 audience recording [14][19][22]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: NFA [1]
- Anchorage audience was hungry for entertainment, contributing to the show's energy [21]
- Management told the audience to try not to smoke during the introduction [24]
- Listener prefers this show's playing slightly over the next day's performance [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-06-20.sbd.bertha.tetzeli.fix-25468.73846.reflac.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller, Jay Ashley, and Bill Tetzeli; source: SBD>>MC>>SS>SBM2 [1]
- **gd1980-06-20.mtx.seamons.92783.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [2]. Also: Recorded by Eddie Claridge at soundboard, patched from Dan Healy's AKG 414 [2]
- **gd80-06-20.sbd.donohue.17268.sbefixed.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Mastered and encoded from first generation cassette by Brian Donohue in Kodiak [3]
- **gd1980-06-20.sbd.miller.bertha.25468.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jay Ashley; source: SHNID 25469: SBD>>MC>>SS>SBM2>>CDA>>WAV(EAC)>>SHN [5]. Also: Digitally remastered in 2004 using a dual-DAW system named Bertha [5]
- **gd1980-06-20.sbd.miller.25469.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master [6]. Also: Cassette masters supplied by Richard Hale and converted to SHN by Charlie Miller [6]
- **gd80-06-20.akg-claridge-healy.vernon.20205.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Eddie Claridge patching from Dan Healy; source: Audience Recording: AKG 414 stereo mic [9]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead West High Auditorium - June 21, 1980](https://www.dead.net/show/june-21-1980) [27]
